hunts.label: Sunday, Nov 15
hunts.subtitle: Second frost morning, same woods, new seat. The squirrels did not read the calendar, but the game warden's rules did.

rules.title: Sunday is not Saturday
items: **Hunter orange is required.** Deer gun season is open for other hunters until Jan 1, and bear season is open Nov 14 to 22. Wear your orange hat and vest.
**Stop by 9:30 am.** Plan to be unloaded and walking out at 9:00.
**All migratory birds are closed on Sundays.** No doves, crows, snipe, rails, woodcock, or ducks today.
No clock change this weekend. The next one is Sunday Mar 14, 2027.
rules.note: Confirm Sunday rules and seasons in the current NCWRC Regulations Digest before you go.

items: Walk-in: about **34F** with frost. The 4 to 7 am forecast runs 35, 34, 34, then 33F.
9 am: about **43F**. The afternoon high is near **57F**.
Wind: **northwest 5 to 10 mph** for the day. Hour-by-hour wind and gusts were not listed.
Sky: sunny early, then clouding up later. Rain chance about **4 percent**. **Frost advisory until 8 am.**
Moon: **waxing crescent, about 31 percent** (calculated). It stays low in the daytime sky, so the dark hours are moonless.
conditions.meaning: Assumption: a second frost morning and a clear sky mean quiet squirrels until the sun hits the trunks around 7:15, then a strong feed from about 7:15 to 9:00. Rabbits sit at the first sunny edge once the frost melts.
conditions.hours_note: No hour-by-hour table with wind and cloud cover was available, so the hourly chart is left out. The hourly temperatures are in the list above.

wind.label: NW 5 to 10 (daily forecast; hourly detail not listed)

in_season.tip: Sunlit feed trees after 7:15. Fresh cuttings on the frost show where they fed.
Sunny edges of thick cover and the feed bins area, after the frost melts.
Open. Last ones going to dens at first light. Take only a sure, close shot.

in_season: Quail opens next Saturday, Nov 21. Not open today.
Migratory birds (doves, crow, snipe, rails, woodcock, ducks): closed on Sunday.
Deer: tag filled for the season. Do not shoot a deer.
Bear and bobcat are open. You do not hunt them. Stay aware near the swamp.

plan.title: Swamp-Edge Holly Seat
plan.why: Saturday you sat in the center of the loop. Today move to the **holly and hardwood cluster just west of the main trail, about 30 yards south of the swamp edge**, near the Junction. Sit against a wide trunk and face **north-northwest**. The northwest breeze is in your face, so your scent blows behind you. The low sun rises behind your right shoulder and lights the trunks in front of you. Hollies hold berries and oaks drop nuts, so squirrels come here to feed. Frost makes leaves loud, so walk in on bare trail dirt. Every shot goes between WNW and NNE, with a trunk, the swamp, or the ground behind the animal.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail, about 25 minutes before legal light. Red light only. Walk on bare dirt, not frosted leaves. 20 steps, stop 10 seconds. Gun unloaded.
Near the Junction, step off the trail to the holly cluster on the west side. Sit against the widest trunk, facing NNW. Load #4, plug in. Red light off.
Legal light. Do not move. Scan the trunks 20 to 40 yards out, from WNW round to NNE. Frost keeps squirrels in the nest.
Sunrise. Watch for the first sunlit trunks. Practice the backstop check (see skill) on each trunk you scan. Do not shoot yet.
Sun reaches the feed trees. Squirrel time begins. Use the leaf-scratch call once, then stay still for 10 minutes.
Frost is gone and the leaves are quiet. Still-hunt slowly west along the swamp edge, into the wind. 3 steps, then 20 seconds still. Shots N only.
Turn south on the loop trail to the feed bins. Walk the sunny edge of the thick cover for rabbit. Shoot N or W only. Never toward the field SE.
Unload at the bins. Count shells. Walk out by the main trail doing the land task.
Unloaded and out. Sunday hard stop is 9:30, so you have a cushion.

items: **In the gun: #4** (plug in). Good for squirrel to 35 yards.
**Slugs: zipped in a separate pocket.** Bear defense only.
**.22 LR (optional):** head shots on still squirrels only, with a trunk or the ground behind the squirrel.
Pack - GRAB: gun, phone, water bottle filled, tell someone your plan and return time.
Pack - CHARGE: headlamp and spare flashlight before bed.
Pack - RESTOCK after the hunt: water, coffee or tea, nibble, nitrile gloves, .22 LR count, fatwood.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot. Not with #4, not with #7.5.
Swap shells in the open with the muzzle north. Count every shell in and out.
Cold hands are slow hands. Keep your finger outside the guard until the shot is sure.

animals.name: Gray squirrel and fox squirrel
paragraphs: The most common game on the property. Grays work the oaks, hickories, and hollies. A bigger, orange-brown fox squirrel may show in the pines.
After frost they wait until the sun finds the trunks, then feed hard for two hours. Expect the best window from 7:15 to 9:00.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 20 to 35 yards. Aim at the head and neck of a squirrel on a trunk.
With the .22: head only, with wood or ground behind the squirrel.
After the shot, wait 10 minutes. Other squirrels freeze, then move again.
details.note: Mark the fall against a trunk or stump before you move.

details.title: Call: hull drop
steps: Pick up a dry acorn or a holly twig.
Drop it onto dry leaves 5 feet away. Do it twice, 3 seconds apart.
Stay still for 5 minutes. A feeding squirrel drops hulls the same way.
Use it from the seat only, after the frost is off.

after: Tip: look for a half-eaten acorn or hull pile under a tree. Fresh ones are bright inside and not frosted over.
Tip: a squirrel flat on a limb is watching you. Stay frozen and it will usually move on.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: Cottontails use the thick edges near the feed bins and the thickets of pine and holly.
After a frosty night they sit at the first warm edge of cover once the sun reaches it.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 or #7.5 at 15 to 25 yards. Aim at the head and front shoulders.
Shoot only with the ground behind the rabbit.
Never shoot toward the south line or the field SE.

details.title: Technique: the 3-step pause
steps: Take 3 slow steps along a brushy edge, then stand still for 10 seconds.
A hidden rabbit often bolts when you stop moving.
Look for the round black eye and the ear line, not the whole body.
Let it reach 15 yards before you shoot.

after: Tip: wear gloves to clean rabbits. Discard any rabbit with white spots on the liver.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Both feed at night along the swamp and around the feed bins. At first light the last ones head for hollow trees and root dens.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to the head at 20 yards or less.
Approach from behind. Touch the eye with a stick to confirm it is dead. Opossums play dead.
details.note: Wear gloves. Rabies is possible in raccoons.

after: Tip: a dark track on pale frost is fresh. A track with frost in it is old.

animals.name: Bear and bobcat
paragraphs: Awareness only. Bear season is open through Nov 22, so you may hear other hunters. Give a bear space, talk out loud, and back away. Slugs are for defense only.

skill.title: Shot placement and backstops: #4, #7.5, and .22 LR
skill.principle: A clean shot is placement plus backstop. Know where the pellets or bullet go, and what they hit if you miss. If the backstop is not certain, do not shoot.

sections.title: Squirrel with #4 or #7.5
steps: Aim at the head and neck. Pellets in the head kill fast and leave the meat clean.
A squirrel on a trunk: aim at the head, with the trunk behind it. Pellets that miss hit wood.
A squirrel on a limb in the open: shoot only if the sky is north of you and nothing stands beyond. Shot can carry 100 yards or more.
Keep range at 20 to 35 yards. Closer is cleaner. Farther cripples.

sections.title: Squirrel with the .22 LR
steps: Head shot only. A body shot ruins meat and can wound.
The squirrel must have a big trunk or the ground behind it. A .22 bullet can travel over a mile.
Never shoot at a squirrel against the sky or against thin branches.
If the squirrel moves, wait. Do not swing the muzzle through anything you would not shoot.

sections.title: The 4-second backstop check
steps: Look past the animal: what stops a miss?
Look left and right: is the whole arc inside WNW to NNE?
Look at the ground: does the slope run toward you or away?
Say it quietly: trunk, ground, north, clear. Then shoot.

sections.title: After the shot
steps: Keep the gun pointed north and stay seated for a slow count of 10.
Mark the fall against a trunk, stump, or fork.
Unload before you cross open ground or logs.

details.title: Why it matters in the cold
paragraphs: Cold fingers and thick gloves rush shots. A squirrel in sunlight stays for a minute. Waiting for a trunk behind it costs nothing.

skill.checkpoint: Before your first shot, run the backstop check in your head. After the hunt, send a note: about any shot you passed because the backstop was wrong.

land.intro: Continue Saturday's scouting: learn the land by what the squirrels leave behind.
steps: On the walk out, revisit the 2 best feed trees from Saturday, or pick new ones: biggest pile of fresh cuttings.
Pace each from the Junction. Note the tree type if you know it, and whether the pile is bigger than Saturday's.
Look at where the frost melted first. Squirrels and rabbits sit in those sunny spots.
Send what you find with a note: message, for example: note: 2 oaks, 40 and 70 paces from Junction, sun hit them at 7:10, new hulls since Saturday.

safety: NEVER shoot south. The house is SW and the field is SE: no-shoot directions.
Every shot today goes between WNW and NNE, with the ground or a trunk behind the animal.
Hunter orange hat and vest are required (Oct 17 to Jan 1). Deer gun season and bear season are open for other hunters.
Hard stop is 9:30 am on Sunday. Be unloaded and out by 9:00.
Frost makes trails and logs slick. Unload before crossing logs or the swamp edge.
It is about 34F at walk-in. Wear layers you can open as it warms.
